body:
## Pull request overview This PR introduces a dedicated `EncryptedItemCard` UI component for timeline items that couldn't be decrypted, removes inline encrypted content fallback logic from individual card components (NoteCard, MedicalCard, IncidentCard), and improves the type-safety of the `TimelineItemFactory` by leveraging the `PlainTimelineItem`/`EncryptedTimelineItem` discriminated union. On the backend, it fixes a `createdAt` sanitization issue for legacy data, improves error status code classification in the update endpoint, adjusts Mongoose timestamps to prevent conflicts with the explicit `createdAt` string field, and refines parent key management during mock registration. **Changes:** - Added `EncryptedItemCard` component and integrated it into `TimelineItemFactory` as a guard before rendering specific typed card components, removing per-card encrypted content fallbacks. - Backend `createdAt` sanitization for legacy non-ISO date strings, improved PATCH error status codes, and Mongoose timestamps configuration fix. - Improved parent key management in `AuthController` mock-register flow, ensuring correct `parentId` and public key assignment for both token-based and non-token registration. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 21 out of 21 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments.
Show a summary per file | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `src/locales/en.json` | Added new translation keys for decryption failure and encrypted entry notices | | `src/locales/pl.json` | Added Polish translations for decryption failure and encrypted entry notices | | `src/lib/api/timeline.ts` | Improved decryption logic with early PLAINTEXT return, better logging for missing ciphertext | | `src/components/.../EncryptedItemCard.tsx` | New dedicated card component for encrypted/undecryptable timeline items | | `src/components/.../TimelineItemFactory.tsx` | Guard clause for encrypted items, type-narrowing to `PlainTimelineItem` | | `src/components/.../TimelineEditDialog.tsx` | Added encrypted item guard in edit dialog, restructured form rendering | | `src/components/.../NoteCard.tsx` | Removed inline encrypted fallback, uses direct `item.content` | | `src/components/.../MedicalCard.tsx` | Removed Partial casting and encrypted fallbacks | | `src/components/.../IncidentCard.tsx` | Removed encrypted fallbacks for severity and description | | `src/components/.../cards/*.test.tsx` | Added `encryption: 'PLAINTEXT'` to all test mock data | | `backend/src/models/TimelineItem.ts` | Disabled Mongoose auto-`createdAt` to prevent conflict with explicit string field | | `backend/src/application/TimelineService.ts` | Added `createdAt` sanitization for non-ISO strings in update flow | | `backend/src/application/__tests__/TimelineService.test.ts` | Added test for legacy non-ISO `createdAt` update scenario | | `backend/src/adapters/primary/TimelineController.ts` | Improved error handling with specific HTTP status codes for PATCH | | `backend/src/adapters/primary/AuthController.ts` | Improved parent key management in mock-register, correct userId assignment |

comments.body:
The translation key `daylog.cannotEditEncryptedNotice` used here is not defined in either `src/locales/en.json` or `src/locales/pl.json`. This will render the raw key string instead of a translated message. The key needs to be added to both locale files.
```suggestion
                                {t("daylog.cannotEditEncrypted")}
```

The log message includes `privateKeyBase64.substring(0, 10)`, which leaks the first 10 characters of the private key to the browser console. Although this code path is guarded by `isDev`, `privateKeyBase64` is a *private* key, not a user ID. The message text says "current user (ID: ...)" which is also misleading—it's not a user ID, it's part of the private key material. Consider removing the private key fragment from the log message or replacing it with an actual user identifier.
```suggestion
                `This usually means the current development RSA key is not included in the item's encryptedPayload in the backend.`
```

Every other card component in this directory (NoteCard, MedicalCard, IncidentCard, HandoverCard, MedsCard, VacationCard, AttachmentCard) has a corresponding `.test.tsx` file. The new `EncryptedItemCard` is missing test coverage. Consider adding an `EncryptedItemCard.test.tsx` that verifies the component renders the lock icon, translation keys, timestamp, and audit indicator.

The string-matching approach for error categorization is fragile. The check `message.includes("invalid") || message.includes("required")` will match any error message that happens to contain the words "invalid" or "required"—for example, a database error like "invalid connection" would be incorrectly returned as 400 instead of 500. Additionally, a ZodError's message string already typically contains "invalid" or "required" text, so the `(error as any)?.name === "ZodError"` check is redundant. Consider using `instanceof` checks or custom error classes for more reliable error classification.
